name: Jay-Z
hook: A Brooklyn rapper who sold his own CDs from his car, started his own label, and turned a young Chicago producer's sped-up soul samples into the sound of 'The Blueprint'.
blurb: Shawn Carter, Jay-Z, was born in Brooklyn on 4 December 1969 and grew up in the Marcy Houses, a public housing project. In the early 1990s he appeared on stage with Big Daddy Kane, and on Kane's 'Show and Prove' (1994). He is often described as Kane's hype man in that period, which Kane has corrected: he says Jay-Z made guest appearances on his shows. When no big label would sign him, he sold CDs from his car, and in 1995 he started his own label, Roc-A-Fella Records, with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke. His first album, 'Reasonable Doubt' (1996), had beats by DJ Premier, Ski and Clark Kent, and a guest verse from the Notorious B.I.G. Timbaland produced 'Big Pimpin'' (1999). 'The Blueprint' (2001) debuted at number one, built largely on old soul records sped up and pitched higher by a young producer, Kanye West, who made four of its tracks, and it is credited with making West's name. That year Jay-Z attacked Nas and Mobb Deep in 'Takeover', performed at Summer Jam 2001 and released on 'The Blueprint', and Nas answered with 'Ether' that December. They later made up and recorded together from 2006. From 2004 to the end of 2007 he was president of Def Jam, the label Rick Rubin had co-founded.
